subject: Learning Methods
title: The Science of Napping
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Science of Napping.

hook.text: NASA found that a 26-minute nap improved pilot performance by 34 % and alertness by 54 %. Naps are powerful tools.

buildup.text: Short naps provide stage one and two sleep, including sleep spindles that aid memory transfer without the grogginess.

discovery.text: A 20-minute nap after a morning study session can restore afternoon learning capacity nearly to morning levels.

twist.text: Napping too long or too late in the day can interfere with nighttime sleep.

climax.text: The Science of Napping matters because durable learning depends on method, not just effort.

punchline.text: Twenty minutes at midday. Learning capacity restored.

quiz.question: Why should naps be kept to about 20 minutes?
options: The brain can only nap for 20 minutes biologically
Longer naps enter deep sleep causing grogginess and may interfere with nighttime sleep
Twenty minutes is the NASA-mandated maximum
